Don't worry, enjoy your vacation, see all the [best point of interest that Naples](https://lovinitaly.com/naples-travel-guide/) offers to you. And regarding the food, just keep reading.\n\nIn Naples, Italy, there is a variegated and refined offer of vegetarian restaurants, where you'll be able to taste 100% percent natural dishes.\n\nThe vegetarian and the vegans can taste good dishes thanks to the best vegetarian restaurants in the city, all listed in this article.\n\nBut even those people who don't want to eat meat or want to try new light and healthy dishes can do it going to one of these restaurants devoted to those people that don't cook products of animal origin.\n\nLet's see which are the best vegetarian restaurants in Naples that distinguish themselves for the quality of their products and ingredients and the genuineness of their dishes.\n\n[1. 'O Grin](http://www.ogrin.net)\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/25dace693a41d3e65f12539a03a247f54e1ceec5b81e4edb93a659f374f16929.jpg)\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/25dace693a41d3e65f12539a03a247f54e1ceec5b81e4edb93a659f374f16929.jpg)\n\n'O Grin is the first takeaway completely vegan in Naples, and since its opening, years ago, it is still the first choice for a lot of people.\n\nLocated in the university zone of the Historical Center it is literally invaded at lunch by customers that well know the quality and the good taste of their dishes, proposed with zero-mileage ingredients, and different each day.\n\nTo note the attention to the packaging, that minimizes the unsorted wastes, the bike home delivery, and the kindness of the personnel. Absolutely to try.\n\n[2. Vitto Pitagorico](https://www.happycow.net/reviews/vitto-pitagorico-naples-72853)\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/85644ffda09dada7caa07f0dc5af4e1138c14052cbfd439494b81827a45976f5.jpg)\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/85644ffda09dada7caa07f0dc5af4e1138c14052cbfd439494b81827a45976f5.jpg)\n\nThis restaurant is located in front of the National Archaeological Museum, and it is specialized in vegetarian cuisine, vegan, and raw.\n\nIn its menù the Neapolitan pizza is revisited in a vegan way with different flours and, among the specialties, there is the pizza with the hemp flour.\n\nAlso excellent the Spaghetti alla Siciliana. You will also find lots of cakes and vegan ice creams among which the \"avocado cheesecake with bitter cocoa,\" on a base of crumble of coconut and minced almonds, accompanied by a delicious almonds cream.\n\n[3. Amico Bio - Un Sorriso Integrale](https://www.happycow.net/reviews/amico-bio-un-sorriso-integrale-naples-999)\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/eaecfad65bb61b2fd9e3a3042387128e82d0cfb6603e4ada91478b847ee51c36.png)  \nAn Integral Smile works in the vegetarian sector from almost 20 years, and it stimulates the bioregionalism, the 100% agriculture disposition and every aspect regarding the ecology.\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/eaecfad65bb61b2fd9e3a3042387128e82d0cfb6603e4ada91478b847ee51c36.png)\n\nThe tables are made of wood, and the atmosphere is delighted by light new age music. Other than the restaurant service, the clients can purchase some foods as, for example, the organic jams.\n\nThe menù includes vegan appetizers like three kinds of vegan salami and fried tempura, soups, second plates of seitan and tofu.\n\nIt is also possible to order the \"only\" dish which includes soup, rice, and assorted sides.\n\nExcellent the desserts and the fruit salads with cinnamon.\n\n[4. Cavoli Nostri](http://www.cavolinostriveg.com/en/)\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/6a22a5bd772142b9c0be7a7a64e27ba077833c7188a744f7ae43f86008c66f0f.jpg)  \nIt's been the first vegan restaurant in Naples with seating and not just take away. It is very beloved for its tasty and colored dishes other than the reception and the carefulness of the personnel.\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/6a22a5bd772142b9c0be7a7a64e27ba077833c7188a744f7ae43f86008c66f0f.jpg)\n\nThe choice of the raw material (obviously biological) is very severe, and they follow the natural seasonality of the products, all of that to get delicious dishes.\n\nIn the menù are also available raw dishes. The flagship of Cavoli Nostri is the vegan desserts among which it detaches a wonderful tiramisù.\n\n[5. Semi di Sole](https://www.facebook.com/pages/category/Food---Beverage/Semi-di-Sole-146335665430396/)\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/52fdd765c21b7c7f564fa2b476a36ce1aeb3d567126b4b5bb2de785c50b312dd.jpg)  \nThis is not a simple restaurant but a macro-bio-vegetarian cultural association. But from the 01:00 pm to 03:00 pm it is possible to access the special cafeteria where will be served vegetarian and macrobiotic dishes.\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/52fdd765c21b7c7f564fa2b476a36ce1aeb3d567126b4b5bb2de785c50b312dd.jpg)\n\nSemi di Sole also organizes some cooking classes that vary according to the seasons. This could be the perfect opportunity to learn new recipes!\n\n[6. Sbuccia e Bevi - Green Fruit Bar](https://www.happycow.net/reviews/sbuccia-e-bevi-naples-51427)\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/e5d01108227428e690fc2acda73eb45fbfa630af42234495a7a312a5cb14c9b6.jpg)  \nBorn just as a takeaway, this place has grown to become an entirely vegan restaurant.\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/e5d01108227428e690fc2acda73eb45fbfa630af42234495a7a312a5cb14c9b6.jpg)\n\nThe various menù goes from the desserts to the vegan street food among which the best are the burgers, with the revisitation of the most famous Italian dishes like the Ribollita.\n\nTry the vegans babà that have a high success between the customers. There is also the possibility to have dishes without gluten or raw dishes.\n\n[7. CamBIO Vita](http://www.cambiovitastore.it/)\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/272a0d4d2bc56fa66691530741594936aae11f6f940b44839d34e7deddd33056.jpg)\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/272a0d4d2bc56fa66691530741594936aae11f6f940b44839d34e7deddd33056.jpg)\n\nThis small place is both a restaurant with a handful of seating and a bio-shop furnished with alternative bioproducts and books about the vegetarian, vegan and macrobiotics kitchen.\n\nThe menù is variegated, and it is written on a chalkboard at the entrance. In general, the dishes are vegetarian, but it is possible to find a lot of vegan alternatives and gluten-free.\n\nDelicious the soups and the first courses like the rice Venere with Pomodorini.\n\nSweet dessert but also white yogurt with various fillings as goji's berries, almonds, and pistachios accompanied by honey.\n\nTo try the fresh centrifuges that are proposed in numerous combinations.\n\n[8. Mangiafoglia](http://www.mangiafoglia.it/)\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/807cb4bc254daffd07f221b43756845a7b1ae4953dca4f25ae7ed9b161c51dac.jpg)  \nA little local that introduces a lot of vegetarian and vegan alternatives without giving up to some meat and fish dishes.\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/807cb4bc254daffd07f221b43756845a7b1ae4953dca4f25ae7ed9b161c51dac.jpg)\n\nAt lunch, you can use the formula that allows you to compose your soup or salad from a selection of ingredients.\n\nVery good the first course like the integral linguines with arugula pesto and tomatoes or three kinds of ravioli and Mezze Maniche with potatoes and flap mushrooms.\n\nThey organize live weekly evenings with music. Good the choice of the wines, directed toward emergent home labels. Good the relationship quality/price.\n\n[9. Rama Beach](https://ramabeachcafe.com/)\n\nRestaurant on the beach that offers only and exclusively international vegetarian \"Vegfusion\" kitchen. The structure is almost exclusively made of wood and the roof it is composed of straw.\n\nThe construction has not been realized in Campania, but in Bali and afterward, it has traveled up to the coasts of Marina of Varcaturo.\n\nYou can choose to consume the dishes to the open-air, surrounded by a suggestive atmosphere, or inside the structure. The best recipe is the vegetarian meatballs.\n\n[10. Piperita](https://www.happycow.net/reviews/piperita-naples-110968)\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/cbb20b7170e3c339791bd543ea3a1fb949d29a800622458b84e67b46bc8c6c7b.jpg)\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/cbb20b7170e3c339791bd543ea3a1fb949d29a800622458b84e67b46bc8c6c7b.jpg)\n\nThe local is a little off the beaten path but with excellent care both for the menù and the reception. The dishes are aesthetically pleasant but mostly tasty. A must is the vegan carbonara.\n\nAt lunch, it is possible to find a fixed menù at € 9 that includes first course, appetizer, and second course of vegetables with a glass of wine.\n\n[11. Officina Vegana](https://www.happycow.net/reviews/officina-vegana-naples-103234)\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/372e2b3c978770b30a4a925868cbd56c273d2dd1338e47d7be4d48baab55afa5.jpg)  \nLocated in the historical center of Naples, Officina Vegana is a takeaway that proposes a vegetable cuisine made of healthy and genuine ingredients, cooked with alternative methods that respect and exalt the taste and the nutritional properties of the foods.\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/372e2b3c978770b30a4a925868cbd56c273d2dd1338e47d7be4d48baab55afa5.jpg)\n\nA small place near the University Federico II, where to enjoy a relaxing and savory break lunch.\n\n[12. Vero Gastrobar](https://www.happycow.net/reviews/vero-gastrobar-naples-91778)\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/397ec211485376fd816570150b5a8166290720ce77a843e29f3afc6992a8244e.jpg)  \nIn the historical center, Vero Gastrobar is a place that proposes vegetarian and vegan cuisine, from the appetizer to the dessert, revisiting in a \"veggy\" key the typical dishes of the Partenopea tradition.\n\n![](https://dmi4pvc5gbhhd.cloudfront.net/2019/03/397ec211485376fd816570150b5a8166290720ce77a843e29f3afc6992a8244e.jpg)\n\nBut not only: so many are also the proposals of international inspiration in a menu that, every Thursday, proposes new dishes thanks to the creativeness of the chef.\n\n![](https://d1go12qtky6pt0.cloudfront.net/images/lindsay-couch.57ffaa17a202.jpeg)\n\n#### Lindsay S. And in fact, it’s easy to find vegan options in traditional Neapolitan restaurants too, as the local cuisine already includes plenty of plant-based dishes.\n\nThis article will focus mainly on the fully vegetarian and vegan restaurants Naples has to offer, but I’ve also included a few mainstream restaurants with vegan options as well.\n\nWhether you are vegan, vegetarian or just vegcurious, you are sure to enjoy the healthy veggie-filled dishes (and the occasional vegan junk food treat) at these Naples eateries.\n\nAnd if your trip includes other part of Italy, be sure to check out my [ultimate vegan guide to Italy](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/vegan-italy/).\n\nTable of Contents\n\n# Vegan Naples Restaurant Guide\n\n*Includes vegan, vegetarian and vegan friendly restaurants in Naples*\n\n## Vegan Restaurants Naples\n\n### 1. 'O Grin\n\n!['O Grin Vegan Restaurant Naples Italy](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%201671%20980'%3E%3C/svg%3E \"'O Grin Vegan Restaurant Naples Italy\")\n!['O Grin Vegan Restaurant Naples Italy](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/O-Grin-Vegan-Restaurant.jpg \"'O Grin Vegan Restaurant Naples Italy\")\n\n*'O Grin Vegan Restaurant Naples Italy*\n\n‘O Grin was the first completely vegan takeaway to open in Naples. It’s been around for several years now and continues to be the first choice for many locals.  \n  \nLocated in the university zone of the historic center, it is invaded at lunch by customers who know very well how delicious and high quality the food is here. The dishes change each day and are always made with local ingredients.\n\n‘O Grin uses eco-friendly packaging and offers bike home delivery, and the staff are incredibly kind and welcoming. They also have a sense of humor and write funny messages in Italian on the chalkboard outside. Ask a local to translate for you.\n\n### 2. Cavoli Nostri\n\n![Cavoli Nostri - vegan restaurant Naples Italy](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%203456%203456'%3E%3C/svg%3E \"Cavoli Nostri - vegan restaurant Naples Italy\")\n![Cavoli Nostri - vegan restaurant Naples Italy](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/IMG_20190117_122949.jpg \"Cavoli Nostri - vegan restaurant Naples Italy\")\n\n*Cavoli Nostri Vegan Restaurant Naples Italy*\n\nWhereas ‘O Grin was the first vegan takeaway in Naples, Cavoli Nostri was the first vegan Italian restaurant in Naples with its own seating area. It has become a favorite due to its tasty and colorful dishes, as well as the warm welcome from the staff.\n\nThey choose the ingredients very carefully and use organic produce whenever possible. The menu changes according to what’s in season, so you can be sure that what you are eating is local and fresh.\n\nThe mixed platter of antipasti is a good place to start when dining here. It includes a variety of bruschette with inventive toppings, as well as polenta squares and falafel.\n\nI had read in an online review that the platter included arancini, but I think the reviewer must have confused these with the quinoa and spinach balls. I was a little disappointed not to find arancini on the menu, but the balls were still quite tasty.\n\nIf you’re into raw food, you’ll also find some raw vegan options on the menu. But what people really go wild for at Cavoli Nostri are the desserts, including the fabulous tiramisù.\n\n### 3. Sbuccia e Bevi - Green Fruit Bar\n\n[A post shared by Sbuccia & Bevi (@sbucciaebevi)](https://www.instagram.com/p/BtWN_CJAJzc/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_medium=loading) on Feb 1, 2019 at 9:14am PST\n\nThis place started out as just a takeaway but has expanded to become a fully-fledged vegan restaurant.\n\nPrices are very reasonable and portions are large, so if you’re on a tight budget this is a great option. The menu is quite large and includes traditional vegan Italian dishes such as *ribollita*, as well as more international vegan fare like tofu, seitan and veggie burgers.  \n  \nLooking for a vegan version of a typical Neapolitan dessert? Try the vegan *babà*, which are extremely popular. Gluten free and raw vegan dishes are also available.\n\n### 4. Officina Vegana\n\n[A post shared by Officina Vegana (@officina\\_vegana)](https://www.instagram.com/p/CAfKibnADZP/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading) on May 22, 2020 at 3:34am PDT\n\nLocated in the historic center of Naples, Officina Vegana is a small place that functions mainly as a takeaway but also has a few seats for diners.\n\nPrices here are also pretty low, and yet Officina Vegana still manages to use high-quality, organic ingredients. The focus is on healthy but tasty vegan cuisine.\n\nIf you are getting a bit tired of pizza and pasta, this is a good place to come. The menu is quite varied, and everything is made in house, including the tofu and seitan.\n\n### 5. Milkaway -- CLOSED\n\n![Milkaway Vegan Naples Italy Bakery and Takeaway](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%203456%203456'%3E%3C/svg%3E \"Milkaway Vegan Naples Italy Bakery and Takeaway\")\n![Milkaway Vegan Naples Italy Bakery and Takeaway](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/IMG_20190117_143525.jpg \"Milkaway Vegan Naples Italy Bakery and Takeaway\")\n\n*Milkaway Vegan Naples Italy Bakery and Takeaway*\n\nThis tiny, all-vegan bakery is essentially just for takeaway. But what it lacks in space it makes up for with a big, warm welcome from the staff.\n\nThe cannoli served here are a reinvented, “improved” version of the classic Sicilian dessert. The cream is much lighter than the usual ricotta and is mixed with pieces of dark chocolate. Instead of the usual fried pastry shell, it’s wrapped up in a light, crispy wafer. All vegan, of course.\n\nIn addition to the sweet treats, you can also find vegetable-filled crêpes and other savory options.\n\n## Vegetarian Restaurants Naples\n\n### 6. Vitto Pitagorico\n\n[A post shared by Vitto Pitagorico (@vittopitagorico)](https://www.instagram.com/p/BeVQLvbDf32/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_medium=loading) on Jan 24, 2018 at 4:23am PST\n\nThis restaurant is located in front of the National Archaeological Museum, so it’s an obvious place to stop for a meal after you’ve had your museum fix. They specialize in vegetarian, vegan and raw vegan cuisine, and the menu includes a selection of dishes in all three of those categories.\n\nIf you’re looking for a pizza that’s made in the traditional Neapolitan style but with vegan cheese, this is a fantastic option. There are many different pizzas to choose from, and they can also make the crust with different flours, including [hemp](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/hemp-new-vegan-wool/) flour.\n\nThis is one of the few vegan and vegetarian restaurants in Naples that stay open late, so if you’re a night owl, it’s a godsend. Prices a bit higher than average here, considering the ambience and the quality of the food, it’s still good value.\n\nThe pizzas are the most economical option and range from about 8 to 12 euros. The pastas, cakes and vegan ice creams are also highly rated, but cost a bit more.\n\n### 7. Pizzeria Da Michele\n\n![Pizza marinara at Da Michele Pizzeria in Naples Italy](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%204032%203024'%3E%3C/svg%3E \"Pizza marinara at Da Michele Pizzeria in Naples Italy\")\n![Pizza marinara at Da Michele Pizzeria in Naples Italy](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/Da-Michele-1.jpg \"Pizza marinara at Da Michele Pizzeria in Naples Italy\")\n\n*Pizza Marinara at Da Michele Pizzeria in Naples Italy*\n\n**Watch the video to see me taste test the pizza marinara at Da Michele!**\n\nThe staff at Da Michele would probably never think to call it a vegetarian restaurant, but since they do serve only vegetarian food, it belongs in this section of the guide.\n\nIn fact, you could even say that half of the menu is vegan! That’s a bit misleading, though, because they only serve two dishes: pizza marinara and pizza margherita.\n\nDa Michele is a super traditional and highly regarded Neapolitan pizzeria that has been around since 1870. Pizza marinara, which contains no cheese or other animal products, was the first pizza ever invented. Pizza margherita is similar, but with the addition of cheese.\n\nFor many Neapolitans, these are the only real pizzas, and old-school places like Da Michele don’t even bother with any other toppings.\n\nThe place is always packed, and you’ll probably have to take a number and queue to get in, but the line moves pretty quickly. It’s almost a rite of passage to eat at Pizzeria Da Michele when you’re in Naples.\n\n### 8. Amico Bio -- Un Sorriso Integrale\n\n[A post shared by Vegan Food ? London ?? (@thelittlelondonvegan)](https://www.instagram.com/p/BlQCo3GgQGY/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_medium=loading) on Jul 15, 2018 at 4:28am PDT\n\nThis is one of the oldest vegetarian restaurants in Naples and has been around for nearly 20 years. The name recently changed from Un Sorriso Integrale to Amico Bio, but the food and concept remains the same.\n\nThe prices are very reasonable, the location near Piazza Bellini in the old town can’t be beat, and it stays open late every night of the week.\n\nYou’ll see long queues outside many of the restaurants in this popular area, but you can usually get a table at Amico Bio without needing to reserve.\n\nAbout 70 percent of the menu is vegan, and most of the other dishes can be made vegan on request.\n\nYou’ll find vegan versions of traditional Italian food here. The menu is laid out in typical Italian fashion with a variety of courses, starting with the antipasti and ending with dessert.\n\n### 9. Vero Gastrobar\n\n![Vegan stuffed zucchini at Vero Gastrobar vegetarian restaurant in Naples Italy](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%203456%203456'%3E%3C/svg%3E \"Vegan stuffed zucchini at Vero Gastrobar vegetarian restaurant in Naples Italy\")\n![Vegan stuffed zucchini at Vero Gastrobar vegetarian restaurant in Naples Italy](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/IMG_20190117_204501.jpg \"Vegan stuffed zucchini at Vero Gastrobar vegetarian restaurant in Naples Italy\")\n\n*Vegan stuffed fried zucchini flowers at Vero Gastrobar vegetarian restaurant in Naples Italy*\n\nThis bar and restaurant in one serves a variety of vegetarian and vegan tapas as well as larger dishes. It’s conveniently located in the old town, and in addition to the yummy food there’s also a good selection of wines and draft beers.\n\nA highlight of the menu is the fried zucchini flowers. This Italian specialty is normally stuffed with cow’s milk cheese, but at Vero Gastrobar they make it with a vegan ricotta that is flavored with citrus zest and is absolutely divine!\n\nWhile many veg restaurants in Napoli close early in the evening, this one stays open until 1am, so it’s a great option for dinner or even an after-dinner drink. The renovated cellar downstairs is a cozy spot to enjoy a glass of the local Aglianico red wine.\n\n### 10. Piperita\n\n[A post shared by Piperita ®??? Vegetarian&Vegan (@piperita\\_ristorantepizzeria)](https://www.instagram.com/p/BpjskyfAH2W/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_medium=loading) on Oct 30, 2018 at 5:46am PDT\n\nThere are plenty of traditional Neapolitan dishes that are already vegan. But if you want to taste vegan versions of some of the traditional dishes that are usually made with animal products, this is the place to come.\n\n[Vegan spaghetti alla carbonara](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/vegan-carbonara-in-venice/), eggplant parmesan and tiramisu – you can find it all here and more.\n\nThe original location is a bit off the beaten track for most tourists but is easily accessible via the Piperita metro station. They’ve also opened a second location in Vomero, which is a bit closer to the city center.\n\nYou can also get traditional Naples pizza here with vegan cheese and a variety of different crusts. There’s lots of seating, so reservations are usually not necessary. Prices are quite reasonable too.\n\n### 11. Rama Beach Café\n\n[A post shared by Rama Beach Cafe (@ramabeachcafe.official)](https://www.instagram.com/p/BTtuavOhewv/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_medium=loading) on May 5, 2017 at 7:44am PDT\n\nWant to escape the city for a day and relax at the beach? You could do much worse than Rama Beach, with it’s lovely beach and pool chilled out Southeast Asian vibes and “vegfusion” café.\n\nThe owners fell in love with Indonesia when they traveled there, and they have created a little piece of Indonesia just outside of Naples on the Campania coast. The café is made almost entirely of wood, with a straw roof.\n\nYou can dine outside in the fresh air or enjoy the ambience and décor of the café. There are plenty of recreational facilities on the premises, so it’s a great relaxing getaway.\n\n## Vegan Friendly Restaurants Naples\n\nWhile it’s great to see the number of vegetarian and vegan restaurants growing in Naples, you don’t have to restrict your foodie explorations to these fully veg eateries.\n\nThere are also plenty of traditional Neapolitan dishes that are naturally vegan, and you can find these in the local Naples eateries all over town! I’ve listed a few here, and I’m also working on an article about vegan dishes in traditional Neapolitan cuisine. Watch this space!\n\n### 12. CamBIOvita\n\n[A post shared by Cambiovita (@cambiovitastore)](https://www.instagram.com/p/BsgVmJmBZHg/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_medium=loading) on Jan 11, 2019 at 11:02am PST\n\nThe food at this cozy café is mostly vegetarian and vegan, apart from a few fish dishes. If you’re craving something other than pizza or pasta, this is a healthy alternative.\n\nThe food is simple café fare, focusing mainly on soups, salads, sandwiches, wraps and rice-based dishes. Freshly squeezed juices are also available\n\nIn addition to the small café, there’s also a shop on site that sells a variety of organic, fair trade and handmade items.  \n  \nThe menu is written on a chalkboard at the entrance. The café serves breakfast, lunch and dinner and also offers takeaway and even delivery. Gluten free options are also available.\n\n### 13. Mangiafoglia\n\n[A post shared by Ristorante Mangiafoglia (@mangiafoglia)](https://www.instagram.com/p/BtTFT7OlgWF/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_medium=loading) on Jan 31, 2019 at 4:00am PST\n\nThis is a rather, upscale, stylish restaurant with prices to match. Although the name of the restaurant literally means “eat leaves”, the menu is a mix of vegan, vegetarian and pescatarian dishes.\n\nThe food served here is based on Italian traditions, but with a creative twist. The lunch special that allows you to create your own salad by choosing from a variety of ingredients is a good option for vegans.\n\nOn the dinner menu, vegan options include the pureed cauliflower, potatoes with cardoncelli and porcini mushrooms, crunchy croutons and crunchy peppers.\n\nIf you’re here on a weekend, you might get lucky and catch a live music performance. The wine selection is good and focuses on locally produced tipples.\n\n### 14. Antica Trattoria da Carmine\n\n![Vegan Puttanesca at Antica Trattoria da Carmine, Napoli Italy](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%204032%203024'%3E%3C/svg%3E \"Vegan Puttanesca at Antica Trattoria da Carmine, Napoli Italy\")\n![Vegan Puttanesca at Antica Trattoria da Carmine, Napoli Italy](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/Puttanesca-Antica-Trattoria-da-Carmine-1.jpg \"Vegan Puttanesca at Antica Trattoria da Carmine, Napoli Italy\")\n\n*Vegan Puttanesca at Antica Trattoria da Carmine, Napoli Italy*\n\nThis is a typical Neapolitan trattoria. They may not be consciously catering to vegan customers, but a number of dishes on the menu are already vegan by default, just because Neapolitan cuisine is one of the more [plant based regional cuisines of Italy](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/10-vegan-italian-dishes-youve-never-heard-of/).\n\nTake the *spaghetti alla puttanesca*, for example. In [restaurants in Rome](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/vegan-rome-italy-city-center/), this dish is made with anchovies, but here in Napoli it’s completely vegan.\n\nAnother good choice is the pasta e fagioli (a pasta and bean soup), and the staff can create a completely vegan antipasti platter for you on request.\n\nThe house wine is a steal here at three euros for a half liter. All in all, it’s a good place to experience a traditional Italian trattoria.\n\n### 15. Cicol’e Ricott’\n\n![Vegan Pizza di Scarole at Cicol’e Ricott’ in Napoli Italy](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%204032%203024'%3E%3C/svg%3E \"Vegan Pizza di Scarole at Cicol’e Ricott’ in Napoli Italy\")\n![Vegan Pizza di Scarole at Cicol’e Ricott’ in Napoli Italy](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/Cicol’e-Ricott’-Pizza-di-scarole.jpg \"Vegan Pizza di Scarole at Cicol’e Ricott’ in Napoli Italy\")\n\n*Vegan Pizza di Scarole at Cicol’e Ricott’ in Napoli Italy*\n\nThis small deli in the old town serves a few vegan items, such as *crostini* and *pizza di scarole*. The latter is not the type of pizza you’re used to, though\n\nRather, it’s a type of focaccia stuffed with escarole (a dark leafy green), capers, pine nuts and olives. The one here is vegan, but if you see it elsewhere be sure to ask. Some chefs use *strutto* (lard), and others will add ingredients like anchovies, sausage or cheese.\n\nThis place doesn’t seem to have a website or Facebook page, but you can check out their [Google Maps entry](https://goo.gl/maps/MDdL6MXFKP62) for reviews and location.\n\n### 16. Tandem\n\n![Vegan Ragù alla Scarpetta at Tandem in Napoli Italy](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%203456%203456'%3E%3C/svg%3E \"Vegan Ragù alla Scarpetta at Tandem in Napoli Italy\")\n![Vegan Ragù alla Scarpetta at Tandem in Napoli Italy](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/IMG_20190117_133734.jpg \"Vegan Ragù alla Scarpetta at Tandem in Napoli Italy\")\n\n*Vegan Ragù alla Scarpetta at Tandem in Napoli Italy*\n\nThe ragù served at Tandem is generally considered to be the best in all of Naples. And that’s saying a lot, because ragù is a real institution in this city and is the quintessential Sunday meal for most Neapolitans.\n\nWhile *ragù* in Bologna is made with meat, the *ragù* in Naples is often meatless. Yet another example of how Neapolitan cuisine is vegan friendly by default. Tandem has several vegan options on the menu, and they are all clearly marked.\n\nYou can have your *ragù* served over pasta or “*scarpetta*” style. *Scarpetta* is the word in Italian for when you take a piece of bread and mop up all the sauce and juices left on your plate at the end of the meal.\n\nWhy don’t we have a word for this in English, when it’s clearly one of life’s greatest pleasures?!\n\nAt Tandem, you can make your whole meal into a *scarpetta* extravaganza! You will be served a bowl of thick *ragù* with several slices of delicious Italian bread. Genius.\n\n### 17. Scimmia Factory\n\n![Vegan Gelato at Scimmia Factory in Napoli Italy](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%202448%203264'%3E%3C/svg%3E \"Vegan Gelato at Scimmia Factory in Napoli Italy\")\n![Vegan Gelato at Scimmia Factory in Napoli Italy](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/Scimmia-Factory-gelato.jpg \"Vegan Gelato at Scimmia Factory in Napoli Italy\")\n\n*Vegan Gelato at Scimmia Factory in Napoli Italy*\n\nYou can’t go to Italy without tasting the [famous Italian gelato](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/gelato-milk-not-required/). It’s clearly the best ice cream in the world.\n\nThe various fruit flavors at this gelateria are all vegan, and so is their *cioccolato fondente* (dark chocolate) gelato. To top it off, they also have vegan and gluten-free cones.\n\nThe *fondente* is dark and delicious, and the cones are good too. The service is also very friendly.\n\nA cone with two scoops to take away is 2.50, but be aware that it costs more to sit at the tables outside.\n\n## Map of Vegan Naples Italy\n\nBelow is a Google Map of all the vegan-friendly, vegetarian and vegan restaurants in Naples described in this guide.\n\nJust click on the star next to the title to add it to your Google account.\n\n## Pin It!\n\n![Vegan Friendly Restaurant Guide to Naples Italy](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20735%201102'%3E%3C/svg%3E \"Vegan Friendly Restaurant Guide to Naples Italy\")\n![Vegan Friendly Restaurant Guide to Naples Italy](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/Vegan-Friendly-Restaurant-Guide-to-Naples-Italy.jpg \"Vegan Friendly Restaurant Guide to Naples Italy\")\n\n*Save this post for later on Pinterest!*\n\n![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%2080%2080'%3E%3C/svg%3E)\n![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/56c1260d3127cae2da66adb6d5210b5990a30e7fbc2a000711f4a93a98f36de7?s=80&d=monsterid&r=pg)\n\n## About Wendy Werneth\n\n### 8 Comments\n\n![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%2060%2060'%3E%3C/svg%3E)\n![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/322f49bdc50804b1c9abf752d3ad8bcf86c29715805f48b30434be7040528f04?s=60&d=monsterid&r=pg)\n\nWhen I was in Switzerland, some of my friends laughed at the fact of vegan cheese:) How is it in Italy? Can we expect pizzas or other traditional Italian dishes that have cheese with its vegan replacement?\n\n![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%2060%2060'%3E%3C/svg%3E)\n![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/56c1260d3127cae2da66adb6d5210b5990a30e7fbc2a000711f4a93a98f36de7?s=60&d=monsterid&r=pg)\n\nIt’s becoming more common! It’s still not the norm, but there are several pizzerias in Naples for example that offer vegan cheese. Though to be honest, when I’m in Naples I prefer the original pizza marinara, which is made without cheese anyway. Best pizza in the world, hands down.\n\n![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%2060%2060'%3E%3C/svg%3E)\n![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/cb50027bc428825c729ee5e854dd28f73fd28c54777c6ac012bbe18d2b5acba0?s=60&d=monsterid&r=pg)\n\nGreat guide, thanks. Do you know if the pasta at Tandem is vegan?\n\n![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%2060%2060'%3E%3C/svg%3E)\n![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/56c1260d3127cae2da66adb6d5210b5990a30e7fbc2a000711f4a93a98f36de7?s=60&d=monsterid&r=pg)\n\nHi John,  \nYes, I’m sure there was at least one pasta dish that was marked as vegan on the menu.\n\n![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%2060%2060'%3E%3C/svg%3E)\n![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/77d78c3e4437ae15af3a93459122bd7fe89d2cd0d9f4e5f7c8fbbe2896625852?s=60&d=monsterid&r=pg)\n\nVery helpful article. My partner was originally from the area so liked seeing here how vegan options have improved. Thank you.\n\n![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%2060%2060'%3E%3C/svg%3E)\n![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/56c1260d3127cae2da66adb6d5210b5990a30e7fbc2a000711f4a93a98f36de7?s=60&d=monsterid&r=pg)\n\nThat’s great, I’m glad you and your partner enjoyed the article! Yes, there are lots more vegan and vegetarian restaurants in Naples than there used to be, although the traditional local cuisine includes some vegan-friendly dishes too.\n\n![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%2060%2060'%3E%3C/svg%3E)\n![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/269539dc655fae53fe4a46a7b0f2dbe8a1802841d910e6aec6e9f87d79a2ef64?s=60&d=monsterid&r=pg)\n\nThanks for the article! Was looking for a similar listicle. Would you happen to know if kosher friendly cheese (i.e. cheese made without animal rennet) is an option in Naple’s Pizzerias? if so, what are some good pizzerias for it?\n\n![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%2060%2060'%3E%3C/svg%3E)\n![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/23581b6f49042a0b57261c7a04854248a3f079a49c47e6bc7c91167343a9c516?s=60&d=monsterid&r=pg)\n\nHi Vidit, thanks for your comment! Sorry, I don’t know which cow’s milk cheeses are made without animal rennet. But of course, any pizzeria that serves pizza with vegan cheese, such as Vitto Pitagorico, or those that serve pizza without cheese (which is all of them!) would be suitable.\n\n### Leave a Reply [Cancel reply](/vegan-naples-italy-restaurant-guide/#respond)\n\nYour email address will not be published. I'm an intrepid traveler, vegan foodie and animal lover. I travel all over the world (117 countries and counting!) uncovering vegan treasures to show you how you can be vegan anywhere. [Read more on my About page](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/meet-wendy-2/).\n\n![YouTube](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/wp-content/themes/nirvana/images/socials/YouTube.png)\n![Twitter](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/wp-content/themes/nirvana/images/socials/Twitter.png)\n![Pinterest](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/wp-content/themes/nirvana/images/socials/Pinterest.png)\n![Facebook](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/wp-content/themes/nirvana/images/socials/Facebook.png)\n![Instagram](https://www.thenomadicvegan.com/wp-content/themes/nirvana/images/socials/Instagram.png)",

      "url": "https://devourtours.com/blog/best-vegan-and-vegetarian-restaurants-in-naples",
      "title": "9 Best Vegan and Vegetarian Restaurants in Naples",
      "content": "### Vitto Pitagorico\n\nWe can’t talk about vegan and vegetarian restaurants in Naples without mentioning the high-end Vitto Pitagorico across from the national museum. They’re a bit pricier, but serve ample portions of food and set the bar high on quality. Their zucchini spaghetti and vegan moussaka are packed with flavor, and their pasta dishes always deliver.\n\n### Sorriso Integrale\n\nSorriso Integrale (Vico S. Pietro a Maiella 6) is a more budget-friendly spot in centrally located Piazza Bellini. Their adorable outdoor seating area is secluded from the noise and chaos of the historical center. They serve large portions of vegetable heavy dishes, all organic and locally sourced. [...] An outdoor seating area at a restaurant in Naples with a canopy of greenery\nAn outdoor seating area at a restaurant in Naples with a canopy of greenery\n\n## Sit-down Vegan and Vegetarian Restaurants in Naples\n\n### Cavoli Nostri\n\nCavoli Nostri (Via Palepoli, 32), in the neighborhood right next to the sea, has an extensive menu of starters, first courses, second courses, burgers, and dessert. Their grigliata mista of grilled seitan, mushrooms, tempeh, and more is a perfect sharing plate for the table. They also have a wine list full of local varieties. You can find something for everyone here!\n\n### Vitto Pitagorico [...] ### Officina Vegana\n\nOfficina Vegana (Via Sedile di Porto, 71) is a vegan tavola calda, a place where you can build your own plate of food from the options presented. You can also make custom wraps and sandwiches. Because the menu changes every day, you can go back two days in a row if you’re a fan!\n\n### O’Grin\n\nNearby spot O’Grin (Via Mezzocannone, 83) similarly changes its menu each day, and has a large indoor seating area. They also indicate gluten free options and are happy to accommodate any other dietary needs.\n\n### OVEN Forno Vegetariano\n\nFinally, OVEN Forno Vegetariano is a hole-in-the-wall spot that’s open for lunch and dinner. Tours](https://assets2.devourtours.com/wp-content/uploads/DevourTours_logo_V2C_PNG_cropped-1.png)\n![Spain](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/spain.svg)\n![Italy](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/italy.svg)\n![France](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)\n![France](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/france.svg)\n![Portugal](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)\n![Portugal](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/portugal.svg)\n![Netherlands](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)\n![Netherlands](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/netherlands.svg)\n![UK](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)\n![UK](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/uk.svg)\n![Ireland](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)\n![Ireland](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/ireland.svg)\n![USA](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)\n![USA](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/usa.svg)\n![Spain](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/spain.svg)\n![Italy](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/italy.svg)\n![USA](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)\n![USA](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/usa.svg)\n![France](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)\n![France](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/france.svg)\n![Portugal](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)\n![Portugal](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/portugal.svg)\n![Greece](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)\n![Greece](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/greece.svg)\n![Netherlands](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)\n![Netherlands](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/netherlands.svg)\n![UK](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)\n![UK](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/uk.svg)\n![Ireland](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)\n![Ireland](https://devourtours.com/wp-content/themes/devourtours/assets/img/nav/ireland.svg)\n\n[Home](/) > [Food Blogs](/blog/) > [Visit Italy](/blog/visit-italy/) > [Naples Travel Tips](/blog/visit-italy/naples-travel-tips/) > [9 Best Vegan and Vegetarian Restaurants in Naples](/blog/best-vegan-and-vegetarian-restaurants-in-naples/)\n\n# 9 Best Vegan and Vegetarian Restaurants in Naples\n\n![](data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAASwAAAEsAQAAAABRBrPYAAAAAnRSTlMAAHaTzTgAAAAiSURBVGje7cExAQAAAMKg9U9tCj+gAAAAAAAAAAAAAAB4GS20AAH/6QlrAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC)\n![](https://wordpress-assets-devourtours.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/ChelseaNewmanBioPhotoDevour.jpg)\n\nChelsea has lived in Naples for five years and is deeply embedded in the community, volunteering frequently with local groups to improve the city they call home. Chelsea speaks some Neapolitan as well as fluent Italian. (Yes, Naples has its own language!) They have a deep appreciation for the simple pleasures of the city – a strong espresso in the morning, chaotic open air markets, the smell of the seaside, and, of course, a fantastic pizza.\n\nLast Updated on November 10, 2025 by [Emma Fajcz](https://devourtours.com/about/) | Published: September 29, 2022\n\nItalian food in general is known for being pretty meat-heavy, and some of the most famous Neapolitan dishes are no exception. Ragù, seafood pasta, meatballs, and steamed mussels, just to name a few. But don’t let that discourage you, vegans and vegetarians! There is a growing number of awesome vegan and vegetarian restaurants in Naples, Italy that cater to your diet.\n\nIn addition to plant-based eateries, you can find some traditional dishes in almost all restaurants that are made without animal products. Vegan and vegetarian cuisine in Naples isn’t big on fake meat or cheese that tastes like the “real thing”. Rather, they rely on the fresh produce of the area to make Neapolitan style dishes that let the natural flavors of the food shine.\n\n![Close up of a vegetarian pasta dish with pistachios and burrata cheese.](data:image/png;base64,)\n![Close up of a vegetarian pasta dish with pistachios and burrata cheese.](https://wordpress-assets-devourtours.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/chris-curry-Fkn8D7DwwEQ-unsplash.jpg)\n\nHere’s our list of the best naturally veggie-based dishes, and vegan and vegetarian restaurants in Naples, Italy.\n\n## Naturally Vegan Neapolitan Dishes\n\n### Starita\n\nThere are lots of vegetarian pizza options, but you can also find a great *pizza marinara* (without cheese) in many places. One of the most legendary renditions can be found at Starita, but tell them to hold off on the final sprinkle of *parmiggiano* if you don’t eat cheese.\n\nAnother classic vegan dish is *spaghetti con pomodorini del piennolo,* a spaghetti dish made with unique tomatoes plucked from the slopes of vesuvius.\n\n**Insider’s tip:** For the vegetarians out there, be careful of pasta that might seem vegetarian but really isn’t. Often restaurants throw bacon, or *pancetta,* into cheese-based pasta dishes that don’t contain other meat. It’s worth asking before ordering!\n\n![Pizza marinara, a naturally vegan dish found in Naples, is tomato sauce with herbs and garlic atop perfect crust.](data:image/png;base64,)\n![Pizza marinara, a naturally vegan dish found in Naples, is tomato sauce with herbs and garlic atop perfect crust.](https://wordpress-assets-devourtours.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/537749176_ddffd02860_k.jpg)\n\n## Vegetarian and Vegan Lunch Spots and Quick Eats in Naples\n\nThere are three well-known and very reasonably priced places right in the historical center where you can grab a filling and delicious lunch on the go. These vegan and vegetarian restaurants in Naples are excellent for a quick bite or lunch.\n\n### Officina Vegana\n\nOfficina Vegana (*Via Sedile di Porto, 71*) is a vegan *tavola calda*, a place where you can build your own plate of food from the options presented. You can also make custom wraps and sandwiches. Because the menu changes every day, you can go back two days in a row if you’re a fan!\n\n### O’Grin\n\nNearby spot O’Grin (*Via Mezzocannone, 83*) similarly changes its menu each day, and has a large indoor seating area. They also indicate gluten free options and are happy to accommodate any other dietary needs.\n\n### OVEN Forno Vegetariano\n\nFinally, [OVEN Forno Vegetariano](https://ovennapoli.wordpress.com/) is a hole-in-the-wall spot that’s open for lunch and dinner. They make great “meatballs” from eggplants, pumpkins, and other vegetables, so you can get a taste of the famous Italian dish with none of the meat!\n\n![An outdoor seating area at a restaurant in Naples with a canopy of greenery](data:image/png;base64,)\n![An outdoor seating area at a restaurant in Naples with a canopy of greenery](https://wordpress-assets-devourtours.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/picture-seeker-MdToH5mdNFE-unsplash.jpg)\n\n## Sit-down Vegan and Vegetarian Restaurants in Naples\n\n### Cavoli Nostri\n\nCavoli Nostri *(Via Palepoli, 32)*, in the neighborhood right next to the sea, has an extensive menu of starters, first courses, second courses, burgers, and dessert. Their *grigliata mista* of grilled seitan, mushrooms, tempeh, and more is a perfect sharing plate for the table. They also have a wine list full of local varieties. You can find something for everyone here!\n\n### Vitto Pitagorico\n\nWe can’t talk about vegan and vegetarian restaurants in Naples without mentioning the high-end [Vitto Pitagorico](https://www.scoutmenu.it/dettagli-locale.php?id=893) across from the national museum. They’re a bit pricier, but serve ample portions of food and set the bar high on quality. Their zucchini spaghetti and vegan moussaka are packed with flavor, and their pasta dishes always deliver.\n\n### Sorriso Integrale\n\nSorriso Integrale *(Vico S. Pietro a Maiella 6)* is a more budget-friendly spot in centrally located Piazza Bellini. Their adorable outdoor seating area is secluded from the noise and chaos of the historical center. They serve large portions of vegetable heavy dishes, all organic and locally sourced.\n\nAt Sorriso Integrale get the *piatto unico*, or large mixed plate, if you want to sample the seasonal offerings. It’s big enough to provide a light lunch for two, but if you’re really hungry, pair it with something else like a local cheese or vegan protein plate.\n\n![Close up of a plate of zucchini spaghetti](data:image/png;base64,)\n![Close up of a plate of zucchini spaghetti](https://wordpress-assets-devourtours.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/clara-farras-XLw_VAgsZZA-unsplash.jpg)\n\n## Vegan-Friendly Sweets\n\nMost of the restaurants listed above will have desserts on their menus, but we would like to highlight two other places for great vegan desserts.\n\n### Vegan Art By Sbuccia e Bevi\n\nVegan Art By Sbuccia e Bevi (*Via Duomo, 238*) is well-known for its sweets and pastries. They have so many different options to choose from, from Neapolitan classics like [*babà* (a rum soaked cake)](https://devourtours.com/blog/baba-napoletano/) to creative *semifreddi*.\n\n### Mennella\n\nWalking around Naples, you’ll probably notice the gelato shop Mennella, which has various locations in the city. Although it’s not a vegan gelato shop, their naturally vegan sorbet is some of the best you’ll ever taste. They always have four to six different sorbet flavors, often using seasonal fruits like fig, mulberry, or apple. If you’re indecisive, you can ask for a sample spoon.\n\n![Close up of someone holding a small cup of vegan chocolate gelato](data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAABLAAAAMgAQAAAAAbm6avAAAAAnRSTlMAAHaTzTgAAACMSURBVHja7cExAQAAAMKg9U9tB2+gAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAPgPX7wABGnGBnwAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==)\n![Close up of someone holding a small cup of vegan chocolate gelato](https://wordpress-assets-devourtours.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/42356096320_9f71c687cf_k.jpg)\n\nAlthough much of Neapolitan cuisine is made up of meat and fish, there’s no lack of flavorful vegan and vegetarian food in Naples. We hope this ultimate guide to vegan and vegetarian restaurants in Naples, Italy has provided ample encouragement for all the hesitant plant-based eaters out there who were worried about food options in Naples. *Buon appetito!*\n\n## Explore International Cuisine Like a Local\n\nJoin one of [our top-rated food tours](https://devourtours.com/destinations/) that are offered in many cities throughout the world! With the help of our expert local guides, you’ll get to see, hear, and taste your way through these cities and learn about their fascinating histories and cultures.\n\n## Related       "raw_content": "# [The Vegetarian Tourist](https://vegetariantourist.com/)\n\n![The Vegetarian Tourist](http://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/New-Cover.png)\n\n# Where To Dine In Naples, Italy\n\nI hope you have enjoyed reading about my adventures in Italy learning all about San Marzano tomatoes (read all about it [here](https://vegetariantourist.com/2022/09/san-marzano-tomatoes/) and [here](https://vegetariantourist.com/2022/10/san-marzano-tomato-edition/)). On this trip, our homebase was Naples, Italy and from there we made day trips to the region to learn about the coveted tomatoes as well as visit the Amalfi Coast and island of Capri.\n\n![Beautiful Naples, Italy](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_6589-rotated.jpg)\n![Galleria Umberto Naples, Italy](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_3893-rotated.jpg)\n\nNaples doesn’t always get rave reviews, but I’m here to tell you I had a great time and really appreciated the city after spending 10 days there. Many people call it the “smaller and grittier version of Rome” and while somewhat true, I’d say that is exactly what I appreciated about it too. I found Naples beautiful, and loved that it is situated on the water with views of Mt. Vesuvius.\n\n![The Streets of Naples, Italy](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_3999-rotated.jpg)\n![Sunset Along The Bay In Naples, Italy](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_3841-rotated.jpg)\n\nAnd, as a vegetarian, you know Italy is like heaven with endless veggie food options. I joke that if you are vegetarian and hungry while in Italy, that’s your own fault. There is no shortage of pizza, pasta, gelato and pastries and it’s available on every corner. Seeing that I was traveling with a group of chefs and foodies, you know we ate at some spectacular places. Here are a few favorites:\n\n[Pizzium](https://pizzium.com/eng/)– What’s actually a chain throughout Italy, I loved not only the food at Pizzium, but the decor and fun ambiance. I sincerely enjoyed all the things we ate including the bruschetta, Caprese salad, margherita pizza and my favorite was the pizza made with San Marzano tomato sauce topped with little mozzarella balls and spheres of pesto. So good and something really unique!\n\n![Bruschetta Wtih San Marzano Tomatoes At Pizzium](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_4927-rotated.jpg)\n![Caprese Salad With San Marzano Tomatoes At Pizzium](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_4939-rotated.jpg)\n![Pizza With San Marzano Tomato Sauce, Mozzarella And Pesto Spheres](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_4956-rotated.jpg)\n\n[Mimi alla Ferrovia](https://www.mimiallaferrovia.it/)– An established restaurant of Naples with a loyal crowd in a beautiful restaurant setting. You can tell the old world charm brings patrons who are regulars. My two favorite dishes were the ricotta topped with a tomato jam (seriously, the lightest and best ricotta I’ve ever had in my life!) and the pasta made with squash blossoms (a specialty of Italy). I actually ate here twice on my trip!\n\n![Fresh Ricotta With Tomato Jam- Mimi Alla Ferrovia](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_4327-rotated.jpg)\n![Pasta Ai Fiori Di Zucca (Pasta With Zucchini Blossoms)](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_4333-rotated.jpg)\n\n[Gaetano Adamo](https://amavery.com/menu/gaetano-adamo/100/?vm=T)– This casual spot near the train station is a great option if you are looking for something quick and chill. Fresh made pizzas straight from the oven are definitely their specialty as are the calzones. They were able to make a vegetarian calzone for me and it was delicious. I was so hungry that evening, I ate almost the entire thing! That’s when you know it is good.\n\n![Calzone At Gaetano Adamus Naples](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_4101-rotated.jpg)\n![Tiramisu At Gaetano Adamus](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_4141-rotated.jpg)\n\n[Diego Vitagliano Pizzeria](https://www.diegovitagliano.it/)– Not only does this restaurant offer atleast five varieties of different pizza crust, there is a pizza lab underneath where they are always innovating new recipes and options. I loved the food here and some favorites included the appetizer of pizza crust tossed with sun-dried tomatoes,arugula, pesto and fresh shaved parmesan as well as the cacio e pepe pizza topped with a pistachio pesto. Don’t skip dessert either, we devoured that chocolate cherry mini cake. A must visit!\n\n![Pizza Crust Appetizer At Diego Vitagliano Pizzeria](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_5276-rotated.jpg)\n![Cacio e Pepe Pizza At Diego Vitagliano Pizzeria](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_5300-rotated.jpg)\n![Delicious Chocolate Cherry Cake](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_5309-rotated.jpg)\n\n[Miranapoli](https://miranapoli.com/)– We stopped here midday during a tour of Naples and only had the chance to get a drink, so I can’t say anything about the food. BUT, Miranapoli is a must visit for the views alone. Situated overlooking the water with Mt. Vesuvius in the background, make sure to get an outdoor patio seat if the weather permits. I relished every sip of my Aperol Spritz and could not take my eyes off that spectacular view.\n\n![Aperol Spritz at Miranapoli](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_6667-rotated.jpg)\n\n[Chalet Ciro 1952](https://www.chaletciro1952.com/)– It was my very last night in Italy and I was tired after a full day on the island of Capri and I needed to get back to the hotel to pack before my 3:30am wakeup call to head to the airport. But, our gracious host insisted that I MUST visit the local hot spot Chalet Ciro for one last hurrah and to try some desserts. Mind you, we had just finsihed a multi-course dinner and I was not even hungry. But, of course I’m glad we went. We each got a delicious, fresh-squeezed tropical juice and then a local famous donut (not sure of the name, sorry!). That donut was hot and fresh and amazing! Ok, it was totally worth it for the lack of sleep before I came back home.\n\n![Tropical Juice at Chalet Ciro](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_7422-rotated.jpg)\n![Selection of Mini Ice Cream Cones at Chalet Ciro](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_7420-rotated.jpg)\n![Famous Naples Pastry at Chalet Ciro](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_7429-rotated.jpg)\n\n[Tarralleria Napoletana](https://www.tarallerianapoletana.it/)– While shopping one day, we saw this adorable store serving these traditional snacks of Naples called tarralli. They are basically breadsticks served in a circular form, but almost look like little donuts. This particular shop had both savory and sweet flavors and were offering samples, so I was definitely intrigued to try a local staple. To note; I learned most tarralli are made with lard, but Tarralleria Napoletana has both vegetarian and vegan options. I loved the basil flavored one the most, but really all of the vegetarian savory options I tried were phenomenal. Highly recommend buying some tarralli from here!\n\n![Tarralli; A Naples Snack](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_4259-rotated.jpg)\n![Make Sure To Seek Out Vegetarian Tarralli](https://vegetariantourist.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/IMG_4261-rotated.jpg)\n\nI hope this is a helpful list for when you find yourself in Naples, Italy. Obviously there are so many great spots, but these were just a few of my favorites. In case you haven't figured it out yet, this article is about vegetarian and vegan restaurants in Naples, Italy, also known as Napoli. Naples has a variety of vegan, vegetarian and vegan friendly restaurants that take pride in offering 100 percent vegan dishes. And in fact, it’s easy to find vegan options in traditional Neapolitan restaurants too, as the local cuisine already includes plenty of plant-based dishes. This article will focus mainly on the fully vegetarian and vegan restaurants Naples has to offer, but I’ve also included a few mainstream restaurants with vegan options as well. # Vegan Naples Restaurant Guide. *Includes vegan, vegetarian and vegan friendly restaurants in Naples*. ## Vegan Restaurants Naples. Fried Rice main dishes available. Many Salads are offered, plus a Duck Salad. Various Soups are also on the menu, plus the Seafood Tom Yum [Hot and Sour Seafood]. Desserts like Banana Delight, Coconut Balls, Sweet Sticky Rice with Mango or Coconut. No bar. Beverages are Soft Drinks, Coffee and Teas. Aqueel Asghar, owner.\n\n  \n  \n \n\n---\n\n![Postcard](dot.gif) ![Postcard](dot.gif)  \n **Long Gone - The Fountain Inn (1923) (1930s)  \n Built by Frank D. Alexander St., **Mount Dora,** FL. 26.2 mile drive from *The Villages.* 1-352-735-8387. **(German)** **[L/D]** Opened September, 2012. Moved from Winter Garden, FL. Located two doors south of 5th Ave., one block west of Donnelly St. Open for lunch and dinner from 11 AM to 9 PM (10 PM on weekends) except closed Mondays all day and Sunday hours are 11 AM to 3 PM only. Decorated with wall and ceiling paintings reminiscent of an Alpen Haus. Only 6 tables inside but twice as many on the porch. Featuring authentic homemade German food especially with a Munich influence. A number of Schnitzel dishes are featured, including two side dishes, like Schnitzel Wiener Art (Pork Schnitzel), Hähnchenschnitzel (Chicken Schnitzel), Zigeunerschnitzel (Pork Schnitzel with Peppers), Jägerschnitzel (Pork Schnitzel with Mushroom Sauce) and traditional Wiener Schnitzel (Austrian Style made from Veal). Käsespätzle (Cheese Pasta), Leberkäse (Pork & Veal Meatloaf), Schweinebraten (Pork Loin), Roulade (Rolled Beef), Sauerbraten (Marinated Beef) and Bratwurst (Pork & Veal Sausage) are also offered. Side dishes like Rotkohl (Red Cabbage), Kartoffelknödel (Potato Dumplings), Sauerkraut, Spätzle (Egg Noodles), Pommes Frites (French Fries), Katoffelpüree (Mashed Potatoes), Kartoffelsalat (German Potato Salad) or Garden Salad, are offered. Usually a choice of two come with the main dish. Additional sides are extra. Lighter meals on a Pretzel Baguette. Special dishes like Grill Hax'n may be available too. Lunch items include Strammer Max (Ham & Eggs), Bratwurst und Kartoffelsalat (Sausage & Potato Salad), Kassler und Kartoffelsalat (Pork Chop & Potato Salad), among others. Desserts like homemade warm Apfelstrudel, Coup Dänemark, Eiskaffee (Coffee Float), Schwarzwälder Kirschtorte or Sacher Torte are usually on the menu too. Kids menu offered also. Lunch specials available. German beers like draft Hofbrau (Lager or Dark), Weihenstephan (Lager or Wheat), Einbecker (Pils), Radler (Pils Beer & Lemon Lime), Russen (Wheat Beer & Lemon Lime) plus German wines, like Liebfraumilch, Auslese, Spätlese and Kabinett, available too. Occasional live music. **Reservations now accepted on weeknights only and recommended.** Outdoor seating available. Achim Weyer, host; Patricia Jarrell, owner and chef.\n\n  \n\n**Older Review:****(from Shelly F. 10/12) Q=5 S=5 V=5 Total=15 out of 15. Return=****No.**\n\n**Review:** **(from Michael G. 7/25) Stopped by the Bistro for dinner on our way to the Orange Blossom Oprey. Seated promptly and welcomed by our server Susie Q. We ordered a Lemonade ($3.50) and a Jim Bean Old Fashion ($8.50). Good conversation with Suzie and she explained a few things on the menu for us and shared the special for the evening. The Mrs. ordered the Special Prime Rib with Spinach and Sautéed Vegetables ($28). I ordered Chicken Picatta over Angel Hair Pasta ($22). Suzie brought us some fresh Hot Rolls and Butter and our food soon followed. Great service and nice atmosphere made the start of our evening great. Total cost for our wonderful dining experience was $84 including a tip.  \n Q=5 S=5 V=5 Total=15 out of 15. Return=****Yes.**\n\n**Review:** **(from Roy J. 10/25) Our group of four arrived for dinner at 5 PM and were cheerfully greeted by Deb, the hostess, who promptly seated us. The restaurant had a warm, inviting feel right from the start. Our waitress, Susie Q, was friendly and attentive, bringing us water and a basket of hot, fresh bread soon after we were seated. We started with the Stuffed Mushrooms appetizer ($11), which was flavorful and perfectly cooked. For our entrées, I enjoyed the Penne Alla Vodka with Chicken ($16), while my wife had the Salmon with Vegetables and Rice ($26). Both dishes were delicious and nicely presented. We also treated ourselves to a couple of adult beverages that complemented the meal well. As the evening went on, the dining room filled up, adding to the lively yet comfortable atmosphere. Service remained attentive throughout and we lingered over great food and good conversation. The total came to $96 before t&t, very reasonable for such a pleasant dining experience. This spot is truly a hidden gem and we’ll definitely be back.   \n Q=5 S=4 V=5 Total=14 out of 15. Sean Langan is expected to move his popular \"bistro\" in the fall of 2026 now. You can expect few changes to the menu and a much larger, 1,700 sq. ft. dining area and staff. Hours are expected to be Wednesday through Sunday 5-9 PM but to 10 PM weekends. Closed on Monday and Tuesday. Reservations are accepted and advised. Corrina Tiffany of *The Villages*, listed owner.\n\n  \n\n\n---\n\n![Postcard](dot.gif)  \n **The Tipsy Skipper - A Tropical Speakeasy  \n Located at 48 S. Magnolia Ave., downtown Ocala.  \n Located next to The Marion Theater. No password required.  \n Discount drink if you have a Marion Theater ticket stub.  \n Open 4 PM to Midnight daily, to 2 AM on weekends.  \n Hidden private lounge behind the bamboo divider. Some outdoor seating.  \n 1950s Polynesian atmosphere serving Mai Tais and Pain Killers.  \n Classic tropical cocktails offered in unique beverage vessels with umbrellas.  \n Beach Drink List. Shots List. Aloha Bowl for four thirsty patrons.  \n Features *Pusser's Rum* drinks and Punches. Happy Hour weekdays before 8 PM.  \n Some Beer and very short Wine List (3!), plus Mocktails and Juice.  \n Some entertainment, like Karaoke on Monday and the annual Adult Spelling Bee.**\n\n---\n\n![Image](dot.gif)\n\n![Not Rated](star000.gif) ![2 Dollar Signs]($$.gif) **[(The) Black Sheep on Broadway,](https://blacksheeponbroadway.com/about-us/)** 128 SW Broadway Street, **Ocala,** FL. 21.3 mile drive from *The Villages.* 1-352-622-1207. **(American) (Sports Bar)** **[L/D]** Opened on October 12th, 2019. Located 3 blocks west of the square, at the corner of Broadway and SW 2nd Avenue, where the **Fox Den Tavern** did business for 2 years. Open weekdays from 3 PM to late and Saturday and Sunday from 11 AM to midnight. More of a bar now, offering appetizers like Fried Green Tomatoes, Chicken Wings, Gator Tail, Crab Cakes or Seared Ahi Tuna. They offer a Charcuterie Board also. Sandwiches include Pork Fritter, Philly Cheese Steak, Burgers, Cuban and a Gulf Coast Reuben. Single Sliders include Ginger Pork or Grilled Chicken, Chicken & Waffle or Caprese, Ahi Tuna, Crab Cake, Duck Confit, Beef Patty or Beef Tenderloin. Soups and Salads, like Greek Grouper, Caesar, or Black 'n Blu are also on the menu. For featured dessert you can make your own Ice Cream Sandwiches. Full bar with a cocktail list. Happy Hour 3-7 PM. **3% surcharge added for credit cards.** Brian Shipman, chef; Meigan and Tony Sardinia and Amy Patice Cannatella, owners.\n\n  \n\n**Review:** **(from Rich C. 3/26) Stella's was closed so we came here since it took forever to find a parking place. No hostess, so we took a table in the front. My better half had a Lemon Drop Martini ($8) and Bacon Jam Slider ($6) with Mushroom & Brie Bisque Soup ($7). I had a Classic Cheese Burger with Fries ($13). Can't remember our servers name but she had a large station. We stayed for the Trivia and it was popular and fun. Our total was $42 with 3% CC fee, before t&t.   \n Q=3 S=3 V=4 Total=10 out of 15. Return=****Yes.**\n\n  \n \n\n---\n\n![Image](dot.gif)\n\n![Not Rated](star000.gif) ![3+ Dollar Signs]($$$+.gif) ![Now Open](nowopenflashing1x1.gif) **[Blind Eye,](https://www.theforgeocala.com/restaurants)**  343 NE 1st Ave., **Ocala,** FL. 21.8 mile drive from *The Villages.* 1-352-230-9600. **(American)** **[L/D]** Opened July 20, 2026. Located in downtown Ocala, 3 blocks north of SR 40, in a brick building that was once a Chevrolet dealership, then a radio station. This is one of the restaurants in **[The Forge at Madison Commons](page2.html#B040)**. It's in the northeast corner of the building. Regular hours are 11 AM to 10 PM daily, to 2 AM Thursday through Saturday. It's a prohibition-era speakeasy, with an upstairs bar and ground floor restaurant featuring American Cuisine. Elevator for ADA use. Live music and a 70-seat bar included. The décor is more \"industrial\" with black high ceilings, than clubby and \"comfy\". Linen napkins provided on hard tables. The organization of the menu can be somewhat confusing. You can find Sicilian Bucatini [Salmon], Churrasco Skewers, Rigatoni Ragu, Miso Salmon, Honey Sage Chicken, Short Ribs or a 14 oz. Ribeye on the dinner menu. Listed at Market Price is Branzino, a Butcher Cut, the Fresh Catch or a 42 oz. Tomahawk Steak. On the lighter side you might see Tuna Crudo, Fritto Mistro, Grilled Oysters, Shrimp Dynamite, Potato Millefeuille and Maple BBQ ribs. Salads include Caesar, Arugula, Verdi and Nappa with Pears. A Flat Bread, Wagyu Slider, Truffle Royal and Tostada Barcelona are also listed. Desserts change frequently. **Reservations accepted.** Limited Wines by the glass run $9-$20 each and by the bottle $31-$70 each. Carlos Sanchez and Wendell Landry, owners here and of the **Horse and Hounds Restaurant** (see [that listing](page2.html#B059)).\n\n  \n  \n \n\n---\n\n![Postcard](dot.gif)  \n **See Silver Springs  \n \"Florida's International Attraction\" (1935)  \n Opened in 1878 with glass bottom boats.**\n\n---\n\n![Image](dot.gif)\n\n![11½ Stars](star115.gif) ![2 Dollar Signs]($$.gif) **Bombay Bistro (Indian Cuisine),** 17860 SE 109th Ave., Suite #600, **Summerfield,** FL. 2.0 mile drive from *The Villages.* 1-352-320-6065. **(Indian) (Vegetarian)** **[L/D]** Opening date was April 10, 2025. Open daily 10 AM to 9 PM, but closed on Mondays. They offer authentic Indian food. Many vegetarian dishes here. Some are spicy. Vegan options are noted. Appetizers include Gobi Pakora, Samosa, Crunchy Lamb and Chicken or Gobi Manchurian. Tandoor Oven specials are popular as are many Egg or Curry dishes too. Biryani with Veggies, Chicken, Lamb or Goat can be ordered. Tandoori Chicken in half and full portions is popular here as is Lamb Seekh Kebob. Naan Bread is extra. A few desserts, like Rasmalai and Kheer, are offered. Kids menu available. Luncheon Buffet offered. No bar here. **Plastic plates and utensils for service. 18% gratuity added for parties of 5 or more.** Krupa, Paru and Bharat Patel with Ankit Dhir, owners here and at **4120 Bombay Café** in Ocala (see [that listing](page2.html#B001m)).\n\n  \n\n**Review:** **(from Mike G. 8/25) This is a newly decorated Indian restaurant on the location the old Pho Village site. Small but comfortable décor. We sat in a nice booth for 4. The waiter was very helpful and described the dishes accurately. Spice level is adjusted to your choice, 1-5. I would call this good but not great Indian food. Nevertheless, we are lucky to have a very appealing Indian restaurant so near the Villages. Two of us are vegetarians. There are many vegetarian choices, and we had an Okra dish, that was pretty good and a Cauliflower dish that was better. The meat eaters had Lamb Vindaloo, which was quite good, and Tandoori Lamb, which our friend said was over-cooked, but with good accompaniments. The Indian Bread was also good. The food was presented well and good Indian restaurant aroma. I would rate the food high 3, my wife a bit higher, so we picked 4, but a low 4. Generous portions. Our bill for 4 persons with no alcoholic drinks was $96.  \n Q=4 S=4 V=4 Total=12 out of 15. Return=****Yes.**\n\n**Review:** **(from Jane G. 5/26) We went here today for the Lunch Buffet. Excellent Indian food. The room is very clean and well-appointed. The Buffet is very generous with lots of fine dishes. There were 3 meat specials, Lamb, Goat and Chicken, 4 vegetarian dishes and several starters [e.g., Pakora]. All medium spiced. There is a large menu as well which you can order from at lunch, as well, if you don't want the Buffet. Indian food is interesting, in itself, but this place also has a line-up of South Indian dishes which are harder to find. If you order from the menu, you can specify the level of spiciness. The server-manager, Kaushik, is very friendly and helpful. Although in a 441 shopping center, this restaurant is golf cart accessible by going from the historic district to Walmart and crossing 441 there. Buffet cost is $17.99 per person. Drinks are extra. We are lucky to have such an interesting place near the Villages.  \n Q=4 S=4 V=5 Total=13 out of 15. Return=****Yes.**\n\n**Review:** **(from Jackie N. 7/26) We sat at the long tables in the middle. Our group of 12 consisted of 6 who had the $17.99 Buffet and 6 who ordered a-la-carte. A little less than half had never eaten Indian food before. I had the Buffet which had a nice variety of about 10 dishes including a Salad, Rice and Rice Pudding dessert. Included were the typical Indian Buffet dishes like Tandoori Chicken, Butter Chicken, a Fried Vegetable, Paneer with Chick Peas, etc. Garlic Naan and a plain Naan were included with our meals. We also had Papadam which I asked for but I didn't see on the menu (it's like a spicy cracker). I had the $17.99 Buffet, and a $6 Mango Lasso. The bill was $24 before t&t. The Buffet was smaller and not as tasty as other Indian restaurants we've been to, so probably would not go back.   \n Q=3 S=3 V=3 Total=9 out of 15. Return=****No.**\n\n  \n \n\n---\n\n![Postcard](dot.gif)  \n **Long Gone - Chicken Ranch Drive-In (1940s)  \n With Car Hop Service  \n SW 1st Ave., Ocala.**\n\n---\n\n![Image](dot.gif)\n\n![11½ Stars](star115.gif) ![3 Dollar Signs]($$$.gif)  [![Video](camera20x20.gif)](bonefish2.html) ![AARP Card](aarp20x20.gif) ![Gluten Free Menu](glutenfree.gif) ![Calorie Count](cc20x20.gif) **[Bonefish Grill (Ocala),](http://www.bonefishgrill.com)** 4701 SW College Rd., **Ocala,** FL. 26.2 mile drive from *The Villages.* 1-352-873-3846. **(Seafood)** **[L/D]** Opens at 11 AM daily. Now Sunday Brunch offered 10 AM to 2 PM weekly. On Rt 200 but 1 mile *west* of I-75 (behind the Walgreens). **Now accepting limited reservations, up to 1 month in advance**, for seating from 11 AM daily, right on their [website](https://www.bonefishgrill.com/locations/fl/ocala). Extensive fresh seafood offerings with daily specials. Some popular items are: Florida Stone Crabs (in season 10/15 to 5/1). Bang Bang Shrimp, Crispy Calamari, Corn Chowder with Lump Crab, Pistachio Parmesan Crusted Rainbow Trout, Grouper Piccata, Pork Tenderloin Portabella and Chilean Sea Bass with Warm Mango Salsa. Try Crème Brûlée for dessert. Entrées like Shrimp Fettuccine to Twin Lobster Tails. Oak burning grill gives their seafood a distinct flavor. Casual dress at full linen/paper covered tables. Winner 2008 \"Best Ocala Seafood Restaurant\" by *Ocala Magazine*. Closed Xmas and New Years Day. **Open Easter Sunday at 12 noon. 10% off food portion of the bill by showing your current AARP membership card. Free Bang Bang Shrimp or dessert on your birthday for being a *Bonefish Grill Insider*.** Full bar with signature martinis and a good wine list. **Corkage Fee: $10/btl. for your own wine.** Happy Hour ends 7 PM. One of a growing popular chain owned by Bloomin' Brands, Inc. 2008 & 2011 Foodie Reader's Choice runner-up for \"Best Seafood Restaurant\" in the Orlando area by the *Orlando Sentinel*. Number One rated for \"Top Food\", \"Best Seafood\", \"Top Service\" and \"Top Healthy Options\" for full service chain restaurants by *Zagat*. Gluten free information available on their [website](http://bloominbrandscms.blob.core.windows.net/bfglocations-menus/gluten_free.pdf). One is in *The Villages* on CR 466 (see [that listing](page1.html#A009)). Leconte Carter, Kitchen Manager; Manny Negron, Managing Partner.\n\n  \n\n**Older Review:****(from Rich C. 10/06) Q=5 S=5 V=4 Total=14 out of 15. Located between 3rd and Main St., near the sign, on CR 33/48, just south of CR 470W, 1.5 miles south of the US 27 \"Split\" in South Leesburg. **Open mostly winter months, October through May, Tuesday to Saturday, 9 AM to 3 PM and Sundays too in March. During other months, just 9 AM to 1 PM, Tuesday to Saturday.** Bistro closed during inclement weather. Call if in doubt. It's open-air outdoor seating at tables under the huge oak tree. Served from a food trailer, not a kitchen. Unique creations from fresh ingredients served in disposable baskets with plastic utensils. Menu changes seasonally. You'll find items like Appetizers: Pita Chips and Kale Dip, Fried Green Tomatoes, Grilled Mushroom Caps filled with Cream Cheese, Roasted Beet Skins, Crunchy Fish Sticks and Poppin Nannies. Salads are popular with \"Ladies The Lunch\" like Farm House Salad, Asian Baby Salad, Fruity Salad, Wedgie Salad, Romaine and a Grilled Seasonal Veggie Salad. You can always add Avocado, Bacon, Chicken, Shrimp or Mahi. A Soup is offered daily. For Sandwiches choose from a 'Shroom [Vegan] Burger, The Beat [Bacon & Egg], Chick Chick Boom [Chickpea & Tomato Cakes], Shrimp Po' Boy, BLT and FGT, Grilled Chicken, Breaded Turkey and Gouda Cheese, Southern Chick, Roast Beef on a Hoagie, Grilled Mahi, ½ lb. Beef Burger, Fried Cod, Lamb Gyro or Corned Beef on Rye. All Sandwiches come with a side dish like Slaw, Veggie, Potato Salad, Fresh Fruit, Fries or a Side Salad. Specials daily. Desserts might be Homemade Pies or Cakes. **Charge for split meals.** Occasional music. **Reservations by phone accepted and suggested for Saturday, or arrive before 11 AM.** No bar, Soft Drinks, Coffee and Tea are available. BYOB. **No Corkage Fee for your own wine.** Well behaved pets welcome. The Farm Stand offers local produce. Alex Reyes, chef; Gareth and Jessica Gentry, owners and chefs too.\n\n  \n\n**Older Review:** **(from Jackie N. 1/23) Q=4 S=4 V=4 Total=12 out of 15. Going back to 1989 this location, on 25th Ave., just a few blocks north of E. Silver Springs Blvd. (SR 40), was formerly a **Shells**, then **Hightower's Seafood**, then **Grille 754**, then **Carmichael's**, and then **Bonnie and Clyde's**. It actually goes back to the end of World War II. It re-opened on December 6, 2011. It has bright red walls, decorated with large pictures in two dining rooms, plus a lounge with bar. *\"Comfort Food With Attitude\"* is his slogan. Onions are the theme here, with most items including the bulbous root in the ingredients in some form or another. Appetizers include a Country Onion Loaf with Buttermilk Ranch Dip or Braised Onions with Grilled Flat Bread, Fried Green Tomatoes with Creole Mustard Sauce, Jumbo Lump Crab Cakes with Mango Salsa and New Orleans BBQ Shrimp with Cajun Garlic Brown Butter Sauce. Soups include Grilled Mushroom or Lobster Bisque and their popular Braised Onion Soup with Fontina Cheese Top. Salads include a Mixed Green House, Hearts of Romaine, Mixed Baby Lettuce, and Spinach or Caprese Salads. All, well described, entrées include two sides that could be a vegetable, salad or even soup. They range from Felix's Meat Loaf, Chicken Pot Pie, Penne ala Vodka or Three Cheese Baked Macaroni & Cheese, Roast Turkey Breast with Sage Stuffing, Pasta Primavera, Southern Fried Chicken, Lemon Chicken with White Wine Lemon Butter Sauce or a Vegetarian entrée. There's an 8 oz. Grilled Mahi Mahi, Grilled Norwegian Salmon with Hollandaise or Maple Pecan Salmon on the menu. At the top end are 8 oz. or 12 oz. Prime Rib au Jus, Country Fried Filet Mignon with Brown Gravy, 10 oz. New York Strip Steak, Braised Beef Short Ribs, New Orleans BBQ Shrimp and an 8 oz. Grilled Filet Mignon with Béarnaise Sauce. Vegetables include Baked Sweet Potato, Southern Style Green Beans Cheese Grits, Fresh Corn Off The Cob, and others. Lunch items are a few of the dinner entrées at reduced prices, salads, plus sandwiches such as a Cheeseburger, Patty Melt, Roasted Chicken Salad, Pulled Pork, and Fried White Fish or Philly Cheese Steak. For dessert, you'll find Belgium Chocolate Bread Pudding and others. **Reservations accepted and advised weekends by phone or online via [*Open Table*](http://www.opentable.com/braised-onion).** **20% gratuity added for parties of 6 or more.** Full bar and a limited but varied wine list. **Corkage Fee: $20/btl.** Occasional jazz sessions. Private room for parties. **Thanksgiving Buffet 11:30 AM to 6 PM.** Happy Hour 4-6 PM. Voted a \"Top Restaurant\" in the area by *OpenTable* members.
